content:
marta: heads-up — after the int8-kv rollout on staging i'm seeing brief decode artifacts when we switch kernels mid-stream. small semantic drift (~1-2 tokens) and p95 latency blips
jon: can you paste a trace? is this tied to cache misses or kernel swap overhead? :eyes:
marta: trace below — it happens when request hits an INT8-kv worker and we fall back to fp8 kernels for decode. timeline: KV lookup -> deserialized int8 page -> kernel switch -> decode start. the switch adds ~6-12ms and sometimes a token mismatch
kevin: hmm that ordering could cause kv-scale/rescale boundaries. did we run calibration with the decoding temperature and seq-length distribution?
marta: we calibrated offline but only on short seqs. here's a minimal repro (staging, sample id):
```
# repro sketch
MODEL=redwood-v2-3b
KV_QUANT=INT8
KERNEL_POLICY=auto
SEQ=96
PROMPT=chat-long-context
run_profile --sample-id 2026-03-15-42 --collect-kv --collect-kernel-swaps
```
\nperf-bot: profile attached (s3://redwood-staging/profiles/2026/03/15/2026-03-15-42.tar.gz)
sasha: quick numbers from the profile: median switch cost 9ms, p95 15ms; int8-kv memory 1.05GB vs fp8-kv 2.3GB; end-to-end p95 latency increase ~7% when kernel switch occurs
jon: that mem win is big but cost on p95 is non-trivial. what's the decode quality delta? any BLEU/EMD or edit-distance?
marta: quick eval on our 200 example prompt set: avg token-edit-distance rose from 0.06 -> 0.09 when swaps occurred (small but consistent). some hallucination-like truncations in 3/200 cases
kevin: sounds like two interacting issues: (1) quantization/rescale boundaries introduce tiny logit offsets after cache rehydrate; (2) kernel swap cadence causes decoding alignment jitter. both amplify drift
sasha: possible mitigations: (A) hysteresis on kernel selection so we avoid swapping for short-lived seqs, (B) cache-aware quantization where we keep a small float shadow for hot keys, (C) sampling-based calibration that includes longer sequences to capture rescale dynamics
marta: tried a naive hysteresis patch locally: require 2 consecutive compatibility checks before swap. result: switch count -40%, p95 latency back down ~3%, edit-distance back to 0.065
jon: nice. what's the config? can we express it as a policy?
marta: snippet:
```
kernel_selector:
  policy: compatibility_hysteresis
  hysteresis_checks: 2
  cooldown_ms: 200
  sample_fraction_for_calib: 0.02
```
\nkevin: cooldown_ms helps avoid oscillations for bursty traffic. sample_fraction_for_calib -> we should run a background stream to adapt calibration for long tails
sasha: i'm worried about added complexity on routing. we should A/B 1% traffic with the hysteresis policy + shadow calibration to verify quality regressions go away without raising unit cost too much
jon: agree. also instrument a new metric: kv-kernel-switches_per_1k_requests and kv-edit-distance_90p. add alert thresholds
marta: will open PR with the selector + perf tests and a 1% canary plan. i'll include the reproducible trace and eval set. tagging kevin & sasha for review. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks, will review. if that looks good we can also try a micro-cache (float shadow for top-50 hot keys) experiment after hysteresis
perf-bot: created perf run 2026-03-15-hyst-canary with config ref r-1347
marta: awesome, i'll kick it off and monitor the new metrics. leaving logs here as we get them
jon: great plan. one more ask — add a small synthetic test where we force a swap every 8 tokens to stress the worst-case path. want to see regression curve
sasha: noted. i'll add it to the perf matrix.
